title: PAR-CIM: A Precise/Approximate Reconfigurable Digital CIM Macro with 0.35-4b Fractional Mixed-Bitwidth Quantization
problem: Digital CIM for DNN acceleration faces overhead from resource usage, energy efficiency, and limited architectural flexibility in balancing precision and approximation.
motivation: Existing DCIM solutions handle approximate or reconfigurable paradigms separately; a unified design balancing precision, approximation, and flexibility is needed.
method: PAR-CIM reduces chip area to 0.35× using layer/gate-level approximate computation in its adder trees (circuits that add numbers)—letting some calculations use less precision when exact results aren't critical. It combines this with fractional mixed-bitwidth quantization, which assigns each layer the precision it needs based on Taylor sensitivity analysis (identifying which layers are sensitive to precision loss) and DoReFa-Net (a method for determining optimal precision levels), enabling multi-bit reconfigurable computation mode so the chip dynamically chooses between precise and approximate computation for each operation.
key_novelty: A reconfigurable CIM (computing-in-memory) macro that combines precise and approximate computation with fractional mixed-bitwidth quantization, dynamically adjusting each layer's precision to balance accuracy and chip efficiency.
limitations: Tested on ResNet18 and custom model on CIFAR-10; scalability to larger networks and datasets not demonstrated.
